text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: p99 streaming latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate-sse (severity: P1). Alerting on-call. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail-latency. Pager: paging maya.

maya: seeing the page — I'm on it. what region/cluster?

ricardo: AWS eu-west-1, cluster inference-prod-03. Spike started ~1785234410, p95 ~600ms -> p95 1.2s, p99 ~8s, errors: 504 at the proxy for some streams.

dave: stack trace points to backpressure in the streaming path. Observed long-lived chunking gaps (SSE frames >5s). Also, envoy shows upstream_read_timeout on a subset of pods.

maya: customer impact? any high-value tenants affected?

zoe: support alert: customer "BrightLearn" reported timeouts in classroom sessions (low latency interactive use). Support ticket #4521 open, they are on eu-west.

ricardo: digging into per-pod metrics now. Found 3 pods with high cpu sys and blocked threads. Logs show repeated "write EPIPE" errors in the runtime when client disconnects + occasional stalls: 

```
ERROR runtime/streamer.go:238 write timeout after 5000ms, client backpressure
WARN proxy/streamer: chunk flush delayed 6200ms, kvcache miss
```

maya: thanks. initial triage: likely a combination of client backpressure + envoy/proxy buffering + a change in last deploy that increased max_chunk_size. Any recent deploy?

deploy-bot: deploy completed 1785233200 - commit: af3b7c2 - runtime: reduce-inflight-requests.

dave: that deploy reduced allowed concurrent stream workers per pod from 24 -> 16 to improve memory. Could be that fewer workers + noisy clients causes queueing and tail latency.

lin: I can take the handoff if you need to sleep, maya. What's the mitigation plan?

maya: quick mitigations to try in order: 1) temporarily increase stream worker count back to 24 on inference-prod-03, 2) disable envoy response buffering for /v1/generate-sse route, 3) apply per-tenant rate-limit window for BrightLearn, 4) rollback the deploy if mitigations fail.

ricardo: scaling worker count: patching k8s deployment to set env STREAM_WORKERS=24 on the 3 affected pods. Command: 

```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/inference-runtime STREAM_WORKERS=24 --record
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime
```

dave: disabling response buffering on envoy (temporary) - add this route config snippet: 

```
route:
  name: generate-sse
  match: /v1/generate-sse
  per_connection_buffer_limit_bytes: 0
  typed_per_filter_config:
    envoy.filters.http.buffer: {"@type": "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.buffer.v3.Buffer", "max_request_bytes": 0}
```

lin: I'm going to apply a temporary envoy local config to skip buffering on that route, testing on canary first.

maya: timeline? how fast can we get one mitigation in?

ricardo: STREAM_WORKERS patch applied, rolling restart initiated. Pod 2/3 restarted, pod 3/3 now up. Early numbers: p95 down to ~420ms on the restarted pod, cluster p95 still ~900ms because of the two remaining pods stuck in GC.

dave: envoy change staged on canary (inference-canary-01). Observed immediate reduction in proxy timeouts - canary p99 down from 6s -> 600ms for the route.

zoe: support update drafted for BrightLearn: "We've identified a transient streaming degradation and are applying mitigations; expect improved latencies within ~10-20 minutes. We'll follow up once stabilized." Want me to send now?

maya: hold for 10 minutes while we watch. lin, do you want ownership if I step away?

lin: I'll take ownership. handoff: LIN (oncall) now primary. Current mitigations applied: STREAM_WORKERS=24 rolled to 1/3; envoy buffer disabled on canary; rollback not yet triggered.

annie: ping product — any active launch using SSE today? We need to know impact on momentum.

maya: nothing public but BrightLearn is high-priority.

lin: after 12min of canary change + 10min rollout, full envoy config pushed cluster-wide. p95 recovered to ~220ms, p99 to ~850ms. Errors (504) reduced by 90%.

ricardo: root-cause hypothesis: recent deploy decreased worker parallelism while also increasing max_chunk_interval (to coalesce small tokens). That increased head-of-line blocking: when a noisy client stalled, the limited worker pool and buffering at proxy magnified the stall into long tail latencies.

dave: long-term actions: 1) add graceful backpressure-aware chunk flush (force flush on intervals), 2) autotune STREAM_WORKERS by queue depth, 3) update runbook with proxy buffering guidance. I'll open GH RFC.

lin: immediate postmortem actions: create incident ticket, tag affected tenant list (BrightLearn + 3 others), schedule a pager blameless postmortem.

zoe: sent BrightLearn update at 1785234620. They acknowledged, will monitor.

maya: moving to monitoring + post-incident. Lin will drive postmortem. I'm signing off. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

lin: ack. I'll collect logs, timeline, and open the incident doc. Draft SLA impact calc: 13 minutes of p99 > SLO window for eu-west, estimated affected requests ~43k tokens, potential billing credit? product to confirm.

annie: product confirms we should offer a goodwill credit as per policy if major customer impact. Let's wait for final numbers.

ricardo: saving logs and exports to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1785234444/exports.tar.gz

deploy-bot: notice: rollout restarted earlier changeset af3b7c2.

lin: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next: postmortem, runbook updates, and small infra change to prevent similar head-of-line stalls.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigations applied, monitoring confirms stable latencies. Please file postmortem within 72h.
